tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Existence of minimizing geodesics] ↗ def:geodesic ↗ def:exponential-map

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold, not assumed complete or connected (with the convention that $d(p,q)=\infty $ when there is no smooth path from $p$ to $q$), let $p\in M$ and $D>0$. Suppose that every unit-speed geodesic starting at $p$ is defined on $[0,D]$. Then every $q\in M$ with $d(p,q)\le D$ is joined to $p$ by a geodesic of length $d(p,q)$; equivalently, $q=\exp _p(w)$ for some $w\in T_pM$ with $|w|=d(p,q)$.

Proof

\sketch ↗ lem:normal-ball ↗ def:geodesic ↗ def:exponential-map Choose a sequence of curves whose lengths converge to the distance and replace each by a broken geodesic with uniformly short legs inside normal balls. Arzela–Ascoli yields a uniformly convergent subsequence, while the local geodesic equation and compactness give convergence of the corresponding initial velocities. The limit is a geodesic from $p$ to $q$, and lower semicontinuity of length makes its length equal to $d(p,q)$.

□

We can now state and prove the classical theorem of Hopf and Rinow (compare Theorem 16 of Chapter 5 on p. 137 of \cite{Petersen}).
